title: introduce-slot-based-emission-scheduler-and-kv-warmup-hinting-to-cut-emit-latency
author: Sana Patel
description: Motivation: Streaming tail latency remains an issue for long-lived connections under mixed workload (short chat bursts + long generations). Observed causes: uneven token emission scheduling across streams causing jittered kernel launches, and transient KV cache cold starts when tokens jump contexts. This PR adds a slot-based emission scheduler and a lightweight kv_warmup_hint API to reduce first-byte and tail emit latency. Approach summary: 1) Slot-based emission scheduler: assign short-lived emission slots (1-8ms windows) to active streams so token emission work is coalesced into predictable kernel launch windows while preserving per-stream fairness. 2) Predictive KV warmup hints: runtime exposes a hinting API where the tokenizer/decoding layer can mark a small set of likely next key ranges to prefetch into KV cache asynchronously ahead of actual use. Hints are best-effort and bounded in CPU/GPU work. 3) Soft-credit backpressure with dynamic reclamation: rather than hard blocking on credit drains we allow speculative emission up to a small overcommit threshold and reclaim speculative tokens if latency SLOs are at risk. 4) Adaptive microbatch resizing: monitor 50/95/99 TTFB percentiles and widen/narrow microbatch windows per-device to trade off cost vs tail latency. Checklist: - [x] Scheduler core + unit tests - [x] KV warmup hint plumbing + integration tests - [x] Performance harness and benchmarks against baseline - [x] Safety caps and config flags behind runtime flags - [x] Docs for runtime knobs and metrics Changes include small API surface (kv_warmup_hint) and runtime scheduler options. No model graph changes. See commits and changed files below for detail.

review_comments: Miguel Alvarez: Nice overall design. Two questions: (1) how does slot sizing adapt to bursty clients? (2) can kv_warmup_hint be abused to overflow GPU memory?

Author (Sana Patel): Slot sizing is adaptive — default is 4ms with hysteresis based on per-device 95th percentile emit spacing; config knobs added. Warmup hints are size/cost bounded and accounted against a per-connection warmup budget to avoid memory pressure.
Priya Desai: Requested a small refactor so that the prefetch worker exposes metrics with labels for hint source (decoder/prompt-cache) and that reclaim path is triggered earlier under SLO violations.
Author: Refactor applied, added emit.reclaim_count and warmup.hint_source labels. Reclaim now triggers at 95th TTFB threshold (configurable).
Oliver Chen: Observed a flaky test on CI (prefetch_worker integration) — looks timing-dependent. Suggest replacing a wall-clock sleep with condition notify.
Author: Fixed flake by switching to a notify-based wait and added a longer timeout in CI profile. Re-ran CI.
release_notes: Runtime: slot-based emission scheduler and speculative kv_warmup_hint reduce streaming first-byte and tail emit latency (configs: runtime.slot_emitter.*, runtime.kv.warmup.*). Performance: observed median TTFB improvement ~8-12% and 95th reduction ~20-28% across mixed chat/generation workloads in internal bench.
